title: Tree Constructions for the l1 Distortion of Binary Edit Distance
main_claim: For every sufficiently large d there is a set of equal-length binary words of length at most d whose edit metric needs l1 distortion exp(c·sqrt(log d·log log d)). The paper gives two independent proofs: a finite tree with nested prime periods, and a tree of circle phases with random prime lists. Together with the companion upper embedding (cited as Thm 8.1), this gives log E_Sigma(d) = Theta(sqrt(log d log log d)) uniformly over finite alphabets. The appendix also proves a fixed-length binary conversion with absolute distortion factor 804.
coverage: Checked every proof step. Tagged-row lemma: the split-row gap count (m-i+i'-1)B >= (m-1)B and combining the two bounds on E. Delimiter code: '11' occurs only at block starts, and the 2l bad-block count gives r_n <= 2l. Finite tree: order and gcd claims; separation, where a'=a uses gcd(Q_v,R_v)=1, and for a'!=a fewer than m/2 primes >= k^4 can divide a number |a'-a| < k^{20k}. Cost lemma: T^j occurrences of each depth-j node, total length M/m^j. Finite Fourier identity. Leaf-mass bound 2·sum wt·H <= M. Exceptional-node detection: q <= 2k^{10k} <= J/2, and the average over complete periods is >= 1. The k^k branching step and the final constant C_1. Circle tree: leaf quantization; the prime-list event (reduced denominators <= k^{3k}, rationals separated by more than 2eps, chance g/|P_k| that the candidate prime is selected); the |S_a| > k case via uniform grid translates; the Hoeffding exponent (checked 121/3200); the union bound over P_v <= k^{48k}. Circle detection: the cutoff Q case (1 - 1/(2pi) >= 1/2), the nontrivial-congruence average equal to 1, and divisibility forcing more than g/2 nonempty groups because k^{16k} > Q. The three cost estimates and their sum over depths, the parameter ratios R/Q = k^{48k}/T = k^{-4k}, and the choice of k from d. Corollary: the binary words sit isometrically inside Sigma^{<=d}. Appendix: random-segment LCS bound and its union-bound count, span trimming (g >= 0.01a), the Konig/Hall decomposition into P matchings, and the final 201/402/804 constants.
sibling_notes: Companion paper 'Finite-Circle-Obstructions...' (rank 393) was also reported as no_gap_found. This paper's lower bounds use nothing from the companion; only the matching upper bound in the corollary relies on the cited companion theorem, so nothing is circular.
